name: Jorah
overview: Jorah was a male figure noted in the post-exilic community whose descendants returned to Judah after the Babylonian captivity. He is also identified as Hariph in Nehemiah 7:24, indicating a possible variant or alternate name. His role is primarily known through genealogical records rather than narrative accounts.
namesAndTitles: The name Jorah means "one born during harvest," reflecting a Hebrew origin related to the agricultural season. The alternate name Hariph similarly means "one born at harvest time," reinforcing this thematic connection. Neither name is indicated as being given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Jorah as a descendant of Jacob, situating him within the broader covenant community of Israel. Beyond this, the primary familial note is that his sons or descendants returned to Judah after the exile, emphasizing his lineage's continuity.
scriptureSignificance: Jorah's significance lies in his descendants' return to Judah following the Babylonian captivity, marking a restoration of the people of Israel to their land. The dual naming in Ezra and Nehemiah highlights the preservation of genealogical records crucial for reestablishing the community's identity. This restoration underscores God's faithfulness in preserving His covenant people through generations.
